Project Overview

A portfolio architecture scenario for exchanging incident information between an external application and ServiceNow through a controlled REST contract.

02

Business Scenario

An external enterprise application needs to exchange incident information with ServiceNow without manual ticket creation.

03

Requirements

  • Accept authenticated requests to create or update incident information.
  • Validate JSON payloads and map approved fields consistently.
  • Return clear success or error responses and correlate updates to the intended incident.

Solution Design

Create a REST-based integration that allows incident information to be created or updated programmatically.

06

Detailed Workflow / Architecture

This is an inbound custom REST contract. REST Messages are relevant only if a separate outbound synchronization is required. Invalid or unauthorized requests exit with an error before any incident write.

07

08

Implementation Approach

  1. 01

    Define a narrow contract

    Allow only agreed fields: external_id, short_description, description, category, and subcategory. Set length limits and allowed choice values. Treat the payload schema as a custom contract, not a stock Table API response.

  2. 02

    Authenticate and authorize

    Require HTTPS and an approved authentication method such as OAuth. Give a dedicated integration identity only necessary roles. Enforce API access and table/field permissions explicitly: a custom script's GlideRecord calls do not automatically guarantee ACL enforcement.

  3. 03

    Validate and correlate

    Reject malformed or invalid JSON before writes. Use a source-system plus external_id correlation key backed by uniqueness controls, so retries resolve to the same incident even under concurrent delivery.

  4. 04

    Respond and observe

    Return a structured result and appropriate status. Log a correlation reference, operation, and safe error category; omit credentials and sensitive bodies. Never return raw exception details to callers.

09

Technical Logic

Field allowlist

Do not blindly copy request fields onto an incident. Prevent callers from setting arbitrary assignment, state, caller, or security-sensitive values outside the contract.

Create / update semantics

For this proposed upsert contract, a new correlation key creates an incident (201); an existing key updates allowed fields (200). A key collision or inconsistent source mapping returns 409 instead of updating the wrong record.

Permissions at both layers

Restrict the REST resource and integration roles, then use ACL-aware access or explicit permission checks for record and field operations. Test with the integration identity, not an administrator.

201
Created a new incident for a new correlation key.
200
Updated the matched incident successfully.
400
Malformed JSON or invalid/missing allowed input.
401 / 403
Missing/invalid authentication, or authenticated but not authorized.
409
Correlation conflict; no unsafe write performed.
500
Unexpected server failure; sanitized error and correlation reference.

10

Technical Challenges & Decisions

Authentication lifecycle

Keep secrets outside scripts and payloads, limit token scope, and plan rotation. A valid login must not confer unrestricted incident or field access.

Error and retry strategy

Return stable error codes and validation messages. Retry transient failures with a bounded backoff policy; do not blindly retry permission or schema failures.

Postman contract tests

Use synthetic payloads and an isolated test environment. Assert status, response schema, field persistence, permissions, and repeated-request behavior. Keep authentication values out of exported collections.

11

Testing Approach

Proposed validation scenarios and expected results for an isolated ServiceNow test environment.

Valid create and update in Postman
201 then 200; response structure and stored allowed fields match the contract.
Malformed JSON / missing description summary
400 and an actionable validation code, with no incident created.
Invalid token / insufficient role
401 or 403 as applicable; no incident write or data disclosure.
Duplicate and concurrent external_id
One correlated incident; conflicts handled deliberately without duplicate creation.
Unexpected failure
Sanitized 500 response and a support trace without secrets or raw payload logging.
